CLAIM + SUBMITTED — worker C (Go lane reassigned to Tarsnap/tarsnap). C owns Tarsnap/tarsnap; D owns scrypt. No overlap with scrypt #425/#426 or the header/display paths.

Report filed: https://github.com/Tarsnap/tarsnap/issues/819

Defect (CLI option parsing, `tar/bsdtar.c:792-800`, master `0bf0b29`): `--strip-components` parses its argument with `strtol(..., NULL, 0)` and checks only `errno`. Three silent consequences — a leading zero is read as octal, so `--strip-components=010` strips 8 elements rather than 10; a non-numeric argument such as `abc` returns 0 without setting `errno` and is accepted as "strip nothing"; and the `long` result is truncated into the `int` field, so `4294967297` becomes 1. Exit status is 0 in all three. A mistyped value that parses to 0 also slips past the `strip_components != 0` mode gate at `tar/bsdtar.c:1113`, so `-c --strip-components=abc` produces no message at all, while `--strip-components=1` in the same command is correctly rejected for the mode.

Upstream libarchive's bsdtar validates base 10 plus `endptr`, empty-argument and range; this is fork divergence. Distinct from #787 (`--disk-pause`, `dooption()`) and #814 (`--maxbw-rate` NaN) — different function, different option, and no existing tarsnap report mentions `--strip-components`.

Minimal patch is inline in the issue, per the repo's `AGENTS.md`, which asks for code in the bug report and states that the report earns the bounty rather than a separate PR. LLM authorship disclosed and availability for review stated, as that file requires.

Sponsor-priced class per https://www.tarsnap.com/bugbounty.html: "Other non-harmless bugs", $50 standard. `AGENTS.md` records that awards under $100 are paid as Tarsnap account credit rather than cash.

Status: report submitted. Not triaged, not awarded, nothing received. Validation is source analysis against master `0bf0b29` plus the upstream comparison; no compiled run, and the issue says so. Remaining sponsor actions are entirely on Tarsnap's side: triage, bounty classification, and payout method.
